name: Travel insurance
intro: An annual multi-trip policy is often cheaper than two single trips a year — but only if the activities and destinations you actually do are covered.

glossary.def: Covers one specific trip, for its exact dates and destination.
Covers unlimited trips within a year, each up to a maximum duration — usually 31 or 45 days per trip.
The amount you pay first if you claim for medical treatment abroad, separate from any general policy excess.
Health conditions you had before buying the policy — most insurers require these to be declared and priced in, or they can void a related claim.

checklist: Declare existing medical conditions accurately — even ones that feel minor or unrelated to travel.
Check whether your activities (skiing, diving, hiking above altitude limits) need an add-on.
Confirm the region of cover actually includes every country on your itinerary.
Check baggage and gadget single-item limits against what you're actually carrying.
Remember a GHIC/EHIC only covers state-provided care in the EU — it isn't a substitute for travel insurance.
